name: states
title: States
description: Screen states that never lie: LoadingState (spinner or skeleton, busy, label for screen readers), ErrorState (alert, retry, collapsible details) and DataState, which picks loading, error, empty or your content from a status and never shows empty while pending or after an error.
docs: One item, three components (`error-state`, `loading-state`, `data-state`), since DataState renders the other two and Empty by default. `<DataState status data error onRetry labels={{ errorTitle, retry, emptyTitle }}>{(data) => …}</DataState>` works with any data library: map its status to `pending`, `error` or `success`. Visible copy has no default: the types require `errorTitle` and `emptyTitle` (and `retry` with `onRetry`) unless you pass `renderError` and `empty`. `loading` and `refreshing` are screen-reader labels and default to English. It picks one state from `status`: `error` shows the error; `success` shows empty when `isEmpty(data)` holds and your content otherwise; `pending` shows the data of the last `success` (`keepPreviousData`, default true), else `placeholderData`, with `aria-busy` and a small spinner, and loading when neither is there or both are empty. `data` is read only with `success`: an initial value passed while pending (an `[]` default, a cache guess) never counts as a result, so the first load always shows loading; pass it as `placeholderData` to show it busy instead. Pass `fetching` for libraries whose status stays `success` during a refetch. `isEmpty` decides what counts as empty (an empty array, `null` or `undefined` by default). Every state takes `size`: `inline`, `panel` (default) or `page`. Any other prop (`data-testid`, `id`, `aria-label`) goes on DataState's root `div`, which keeps its own `data-slot`, `data-status` and `aria-busy`.
